review_kind: Codex-assisted answer review; not a human review or paid LLM-judge run
criteria_policy: Exact frozen descriptions and all-three-plus-no-material-defect task-pass rule retained. Overview completed-turn timing is scored for the benchmark despite exceeding its literal question. The separate unprefixed preset is assessed only against the actual question. Historical grades are preserved.
scope: First recorded UI answers only. Source support, Python syntax and code/history behavior inspected statically; no generated code, provider requests, paid judges or remote integrations executed by this review.

criteria.description: Explains the distinct roles of tracing, dataset-based evaluation, and Signals and how they can be used together.
criteria.reason: Only tracing and evaluation facts survive. Signals and a relationship among all three concepts are absent.

criteria.description: Explains that Signals score completed turns; does not confuse their execution timing with an inline answer-release check.
criteria.reason: No explanation of completed-turn Signal timing is supplied.

criteria.description: Does not claim monitoring prevents errors, proves correctness, or guarantees safety.
criteria.reason: No claim of error prevention, correctness proof or guaranteed safety is made.

tasks.source_review: All three retained passages support the delivered facts, but source support does not make the task complete.
caveats: The final answer is explicitly labelled partial, so it does not falsely advertise completeness. It nevertheless fails the user request because Signals and the relationship among all three are absent.
The frozen completed-turn timing requirement exceeds the literal question; this run fails the ordinary relationship criterion as well, independently of that stricter requirement.
The recovery extractor repeats each citation marker. This is cosmetic and does not determine the grade.

criteria.description: Recommends appropriate Op input/output postprocessing hooks to change recorded representations without changing the business function.
criteria.reason: Recommends the correct postprocess_inputs and postprocess_output Op hooks for the recorded representation.

criteria.description: Explains that the input callback receives and returns an argument dictionary, while the output callback transforms the normal return value.
criteria.reason: Explains the input name/value dictionary and the normal return-value transformation.

criteria.description: Describes a suitable masking or omission approach that preserves the real function inputs and behavior. Code is optional; supplied code must implement the described behavior.
criteria.reason: Supplied code omits the recorded password argument and builds a separate masked output without mutating the actual function inputs or result.

tasks.source_review: The callback contracts and Python example follow the exact read Customize logged inputs and outputs passage. TypeScript scope is explicitly limited to the documentation.
tasks.code_behavior_review: The input dictionary comprehension makes a new dictionary without hide_me. The output callback makes a separate CustomObject with the password replaced, while the business function receives and uses the real value. Python parses. No generated code was executed.
caveats: No remote recording or production privacy guarantee is established by this static review.

criteria.description: Explains the mapping from dataset fields to agent or prediction inputs and from predictions plus relevant reference fields to scorer inputs.
criteria.reason: Maps dataset user_request to the agent, reply to prediction output, and task success criteria plus transcript to the judge.

criteria.description: Gives a usable documented evaluation invocation or concrete API-level procedure; accept equivalent supported APIs rather than requiring one particular evaluation class.
criteria.reason: Provides the documented EvaluationLogger/log_prediction/log_score/log_summary procedure and explains its helper boundaries.

criteria.description: Describes a task-relevant LLM judge rubric and how its scores or reasons are recorded or reviewed, without presenting the verdict as certain. An unsolicited fallibility lecture is not required.
criteria.reason: Defines task completion against the request and success criteria, records passed/reason, and explains where to inspect them. No certainty guarantee is asserted.

tasks.source_review: The task dictionaries, transcript judge, EvaluationLogger loop, and result inspection instructions match agent-evals section 4. Placeholder/import explanations match section 3.
tasks.code_behavior_review: Python fragment parses. Each task is recorded as inputs, its user_request enters the agent, the reply becomes pred.output, and task plus transcript enter the judge. Helpers/imports remain explicitly supplied by the cited tutorial. No full loop is claimed or executed.
caveats: The dataset string is the logger reference/name in this documented procedure; the actual task iteration is explicit. This review does not establish remote dataset publication or UI linkage.
No judge model or generated evaluation code was executed by this review.

criteria.description: Across both turns, retains the direct-Anthropic, Python, custom-loop context and gives appropriate conversation/turn/model/tool instrumentation; does not confuse tracing identity with LLM memory.
criteria.reason: Retains Python/direct-Anthropic/custom-loop context, gives conversation/turn/model/tool nesting, and explicitly says tracing does not replace model message history.

criteria.description: Explains how to record model identity and input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation usage on the model span using suitable documented APIs or adapters; does not silently switch to an OpenAI-only response schema.
criteria.reason: Explains the correct Usage fields, concrete response_model and per-model-call recording. The explanatory mapping passes; the separate material code defect below prevents overall task success.

criteria.description: Handles provider-to-Weave input totals without double counting cache tokens, distinguishes cached categories where available, and does not fabricate exact dollar costs. If conversation or tool-call code is supplied, it must preserve the relevant preceding assistant messages.
criteria.reason: Adds input plus cache-read plus cache-creation exactly once, preserves cache categories and does not fabricate costs. Placeholder history is not replaced with an invalid assistant/tool sequence.

tasks.source_review: The nesting and manual instrumentation fragment follow trace-agents/agent-evals; token accounting follows custom-agents-quickstart section 8. Exact source correspondence does not establish applicability to every Anthropic response block.
tasks.code_behavior_review: Both Python fragments parse. They explicitly leave the loop and message history to the application. Cache totals include uncached input plus read plus creation exactly once. However, the follow-up reads resp.content[0].text before recording usage and recommends this for every model call in the custom tool loop. ToolUseBlock and ThinkingBlock have no text field, so those valid response shapes can fail before the requested usage record.
caveats: Minor inherited documentation imprecision: a Conversation groups turns; it does not itself emit a span, despite the quoted Conversation span wording. The actual context nesting remains appropriate.
Cache counts are nullable in the installed Anthropic Usage schema; direct addition needs adaptation if a provider returns None. No such response was executed in this review.

The prior V1 answer explicitly limited its copied snippet to text and said tool-use handling was unchecked. V2 says only single call/not full loop and then recommends the pattern for every tool-loop model call. Historical V1 grades remain unchanged.
No generated code or provider call was executed. Failure reasoning uses the supplied statement order and installed SDK block field definitions.

material_code_defects.location: turn 2 Python fence: llm.output(resp.content[0].text), before llm.record(...)
material_code_defects.claim_scope: Follow-up recommends this pattern for every messages.create call in the custom tool loop.
material_code_defects.failure_condition: The first content block is a ToolUseBlock or ThinkingBlock.
material_code_defects.impact: Accessing .text on either block fails before usage is recorded; relevant to the requested direct-Anthropic tool loop.
material_code_defects.evidence: Installed anthropic.types.ToolUseBlock fields are caller,id,input,name,toolset_name,type; ThinkingBlock fields are signature,thinking,type. Neither exposes text.
material_code_defects.grading: The three requested explanation outcomes pass, but the frozen task-pass rule additionally requires no material code defect preventing the requested use.

history_review.clarification: Retained app dialogue is verified; execution of a generated complete agent loop is not demonstrated.

cache_arithmetic_review.formula: Weave inclusive input = Anthropic input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens
cache_arithmetic_review.scope: Arithmetic illustration of supplied formula, not measured provider usage.

criteria.description: Does not present weave.enable_hallucination_free_mode() as a real supported API; scopes documentation absence claims to the evidence available.
criteria.reason: Does not invent the requested API and limits its absence claim to searched documentation.

criteria.reason: Offers documented hallucination scoring, evaluation and guardrail options with cited scope and no guarantee.

tasks.source_review: HallucinationFreeScorer import, customization, context mapping and Evaluation usage match S1. Inline guardrail intervention and control-flow effects match S2 body/context. Documentation absence is scoped to searched/read material.
tasks.code_behavior_review: Only short inline API examples are supplied; no Python fence or invented hallucination-free API call.
caveats: No scorer, guardrail or remote evaluation executed.

criteria.reason: Distinguishes explicit v3 from name-only latest and explains version/alias forms.

criteria.reason: Says get loads the referenced stored prompt and supplies both calls.

criteria.reason: Requires init for both shorthand forms and explains that a fully qualified URI does not require it.

tasks.source_review: The version/latest/init/qualified-ref rules match the retrieved prompt-version section. Its supplied page context supports immutable published versions.
tasks.code_behavior_review: Short Python example parses and initializes the project before either shorthand ref.get call. Full URI syntax is explicitly not supplied, and is not needed to answer whether init is required.
caveats: No object retrieval, project access or trace export tested by this static review.

separate_preset.question: How do tracing, evaluations, and Signals fit together?
separate_preset.reason: Provides distinct tracing/evaluation/Signals roles and a useful combined development/production workflow. It explicitly labels the cross-page synthesis and suggested workflow as interpretation and separates the deprecated Monitors workflow. No material unsupported claim was demonstrated.
caveats: The pre-release measurement heading describes a useful evaluation use case, not an exclusive product lifecycle; the answer clarifies the workflow is its interpretation.
Completed-turn timing is not supplied, but the literal preset does not request it. This separate pass does not change the benchmark overview criterion or its grade.
No code is supplied; source support was checked against four exact read passages.

summary.decision: Four of six tasks pass the full frozen task rule; sixteen of eighteen requested outcomes pass. All seven UI turns visibly completed, but the benchmark overview delivered a partial answer omitting Signals. The follow-up explains correct accounting yet contains a material tool-response applicability defect. The additional unprefixed preset separately fulfills its literal request.
summary.task_vs_outcome_rule: Follow-up receives three outcome passes for correct explanations, but fails the independent material-code-defect condition. Thus 16/18 outcomes does not imply 5/6 task passes.
summary.comparison_limit: One replay of reused development tasks, with selected prior failures and model nondeterminism; no causal or general superiority claim. Prior app and Claude grades remain unchanged.
